definitions: To anticipate and address a potential problem or situation before it becomes widely known or problematic.
To take proactive measures to control a narrative or situation before others do.
examples: The company tried to get out ahead of the scandal by releasing a statement early.
She always gets out ahead of her competitors by innovating constantly.
We need to get out ahead of the rumors before they spread too far.
pastTenses: got out ahead of (past simple), gotten out ahead of (past perfect)
